item.title: UCL: Bayern sweat over Kompany, Neuer, Kimmich fitness for Arsenal clash
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich could be without manager Vincent Kompany, goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and midfielder Joshua Kimmich for Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Arsenal, assistant coach Aaron Danks has said. According to Reuters, Danks disclosed the doubts at a press conference on Tuesday, with Kompany battling a virus, Neuer recovering from a minor injury and Kimmich missing training for personal reasons. “Vince has had a virus, and it is important for him to rest,” Danks said, adding that the manager was at home and his involvement would be assessed on a day-to-day basis. Neuer has returned to training over the past two days, but Bayern are yet to decide whether the goalkeeper will be available for the Arsenal encounter. Kimmich’s participation also remains uncertain. Bayern will also be without suspended winger Michael Olise as they seek to return to winning ways in the competition after last week’s 3-3 draw against Viking in Norway. However, the German champions head into the encounter with confidence after thrashing RB Leipzig 6-1 in the Bundesliga on Saturday. Danks said the contest would be decided by fine margins, insisting Bayern must prepare for every aspect of the game and encourage their players to perform without fear. Gardephe after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit computer intrusions and conspiracy to commit wire fraud. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has described President Bola Tinubu as “the Egypt Nigerians are desperate to escape,” accusing him of worsening hardship through fuel subsidy removal. Atiku said Tinubu’s comparison of subsidy relief to asking Moses to return to Egypt was out of touch with Nigerians struggling to afford food, transport and other necessities. In a statement on Tuesday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku also faulted Tinubu’s handling of insecurity and police welfare, warning that the President had no business seeking another term without addressing the country’s mounting challenges. “Bola, you are the Egypt Nigerians are desperate to escape. You celebrate the day you made fuel more expensive, then lecture families struggling to pay for food and transport about why they must never go back,” he said. Atiku proposed targeted support for verified petroleum products refined in Nigeria, with imported fuel excluded and independent auditors monitoring the funds to ensure consumers benefit from lower prices. “My proposal is clear: give limited, budgeted support only to verified petroleum products refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians. The lawmaker noted that NAFDAC was statutorily responsible for regulating food, bottled water and other products under its mandate, while the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) was responsible for consumer protection and product safety. The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) also plays a key role in ensuring that products meet applicable standards. He acknowledged the efforts of the three agencies but said concerns persisted over the circulation of products bearing misleading or deceptive information, particularly regarding production and expiry dates, batch numbers, manufacturers’ details and ingredients. The All Progressives Congress lawmaker said existing laws and regulations provided a basis for dealing with unsafe products, but called for stronger enforcement, improved coordination among regulatory agencies, better market surveillance and greater public awareness. He warned that the circulation of fake and substandard food and drinks posed particular risks to children, older people and other vulnerable groups, potentially contributing to foodborne illnesses, poisoning and other preventable health problems. “The House is disturbed that with the presence of NAFDAC, SON, FCCPC, the Police, NSCDC, the increasing circulation of fake and substandard food and drinks is a very disturbing development which calls for more legislative and executive actions,” he said. “We recognise the need for more effective, efficient and better-coordinated result oriented surveillance, inspection, enforcement and timely prosecution throughout the food and beverage supply chain to rid the country of counterfeit and sub-standard products.” Following the adoption of the motion, the House urged the Federal Government to treat the production and circulation of fake, adulterated, counterfeit and substandard food and beverages as a matter of urgent national importance requiring sustained regulatory attention. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, for consideration and approval. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services alongside the Federal Police Service as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. Presenting the committee’s report, its chairman and member representing Qua’an-Pan South Constituency, Theodore Maiyaki, said the proposed amendment was necessary in view of prevailing security challenges, manpower shortages in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen policing at the grassroots. He explained that the proposal would establish a framework for federal and state policing, with safeguards for human rights, operational standards, accountability and coordination. The committee also noted that improved security was critical to the socioeconomic development of Plateau State and the country at large, recommending that the House support the proposed constitutional alteration. Following deliberations, lawmakers adopted the recommendations and voted in support of the proposed amendment. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, commended the committee for its work and thanked members for their patience, commitment and sacrifice in considering the legislative proposal. The constitutional amendment requires approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly before it can proceed to the next stage of the process. Meanwhile, the House passed two other bills for first reading: the Plateau State Right of Patients and Medical Institutions Bill and the Plateau State Bill on Jungle Justice, Mob Action and Other Forms of Unlawful Violence Against Persons. The bills will undergo further legislative consideration in line with the rules of the Assembly. The House subsequently resolved to proceed on recess from Monday, October 19, to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, to allow members to rest and prepare for upcoming legislative responsibilities. The Speaker appreciated lawmakers, supporting staff, and other personnel for their dedication to the service of Plateau State, noting that the Assembly had continued its legislative duties beyond the initially scheduled recess period. item.title: Seven-Up Bottling Company Confirms Authenticity of Yellow Covers as Part of an Exciting Initiative
item.description: Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) has sparked curiosity among consumers with the appearance of bright yellow covers on plastic bottles of key brands, including Pepsi, Mirinda, 7UP, Teem, and Supa Komando. The yellow covers are authentic packaging as a temporary feature in an upcoming initiative the company says will bring something exciting to consumers like never before in selected regions. Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) began building anticipation through a teaser communication alluding to the distinctive yellow covers appearing on bottles in retail outlets, prompting questions about what is coming next. An Instagram post on Pepsi’s Instagram page reinforced the intrigue, promising consumers that “Something exciting is Coming.” The message appears to resonate with consumers, judging by reactions to its social media post. Comments range from expressions of excitement to playful encouragement, with users eager to see what the beverage company has planned. “Let’s gooooo ,” commented verified Instagram user the_obinnan, while eromz.thecreator described the development as “Too activeeeee my favorite drinkkkkkkk.” Another user, mustapha_shi2, added, “Bring it on .” The reactions suggest that the yellow covers have become more than a packaging change in the eyes of consumers. They have become clues in a developing brand mystery, encouraging people to watch for the next announcement and speculate about what the company has in store. While Seven-up Bottling Company has yet to disclose the details of the upcoming initiative, its teaser messaging suggests that the yellow covers are part of a wider campaign designed to build excitement ahead of the reveal. For now, consumers are left watching, guessing and waiting to find out what lies behind the bright yellow covers. item.title: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen govt camp rises to 73
item.description: Local Yemeni authorities on Tuesday raised the death toll from a Houthi strike a day earlier on a military camp belonging to government forces to 73, as fighting between the foes escalates. It marked the deadliest attack in weeks as fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-supported government rages after the collapse of a years-long truce. The death toll from Monday’s strike on the camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province “increased to 73 martyrs, while search and follow-up efforts are ongoing to discover the fate of 14 missing people”, provincial authorities said in a statement. Local authorities had put the death toll at 53 on Monday, adding that more than 200 others were injured, all new members of the internal security forces who were undergoing training. Majed al-Nuzaili, spokesperson for the Yemeni armed forces, stated Monday on X that the Houthis targeted Shabwa with three ballistic missiles, and that the attack “struck a training center for personnel of security and police agencies.” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree later confirmed that the group was responsible for the attack, saying it targeted “Saudi enemy gatherings in Al-Alam camp, which is run by a Saudi officer from the eastern regions”. Shabwa contains major oil and gas fields and is home to the Balhaf liquefied natural gas terminal, the country’s largest energy facility and a key economic asset. A government military source in the province on Monday said the army feared the strikes could pave the way for a ground offensive “similar to what happened in Mokha”, the strategic Red Sea port city seized by the Houthis last month. In a statement responding to Atiku’s call for answers, the presidential aide recalled that the former vice president visited Buhari in Daura, Katsina State, on June 22, 2024, and again at his retirement residence in Kaduna on April 11, 2025. “Those two opportunities presented you with chances to ask former President Buhari, who was President at the time of the Lekki Toll Gate protests, the questions you are now asking President Tinubu,” Olusegun said. item.title: Cash-out delays are turning excitement into suspicion
item.description: It used to be that the thrill of a win was almost instant—a rush followed by quick cash in your account. Now, more and more online gamblers are noticing something different. The wait for payouts is stretching longer than expected, and that pause is starting to feel uncomfortable. For many in Nigeria and beyond, what should be a celebration quickly turns into a tense waiting game. Across social media and gambling forums, players are sharing their frustrations, comparing notes, and wondering why the money isn’t showing up. The joy of betting is changing, as doubts creep in about what’s really happening behind those delayed withdrawals. From anticipation to unease: how winning feels different when payouts stall Instead of the usual thrill that comes right after a win, many players now feel an uneasy pause as they wait for their money to clear. item.title: My mission is to demonstrate power; I don’t collect tithes – Odumeje
item.description: General Overseer of Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry, Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje, has said his ministry does not collect tithes, insisting that his primary mission is to demonstrate spiritual power. The cleric disclosed this during an appearance on the Honest Bunch Podcast, in an episode uploaded to YouTube on Monday. Odumeje criticised churches that frequently preach about tithing, accusing some of prioritising money collection over demonstrating spiritual power and performing miracles. He said, “Those people that collect tithes and teach tithes every day when you come to church, they will be interested in making sure that they clear your pockets. And there is no practical evidence and miracles that you will see. The only thing is stories. That is not the kind of church I run.” Explaining his ministry’s focus, he added, “My mission on earth is demonstration of power. All the teaching of tithe and teaching of giving, I am not in that area.” However, Odumeje clarified that he did not consider tithing wrong, maintaining that the decision to pay should be left to individuals and their relationship with God. “I don’t collect tithes. Nobody pays me tithes. I am not saying that tithe is bad. It’s a decision between you and God if you want to pay tithe. Tithe is real. But it is something that you must decide. Not something that somebody will be brainwashing you, forcing you,” he said. The cleric also condemned teachings suggesting that Christians would be denied access to heaven if they failed to pay tithes. Folarin, who returned to the country from an overseas trip, made the declaration on Monday, appealing to aggrieved party members to put their differences behind them and unite for the common goal of securing electoral victories for the APC. item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Tuesday, declined to declare vacant the seat of the House of Representatives member for Igabi Federal Constituency of Kaduna State, Hussaini Jallo, following his alleged defection to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice James Omotosho, held that the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) failed to provide any credible evidence to prove Jallo’s defection. It held that although the PDP has the legal right to institute the action as a necessary party, it was unable to establish that the lawmaker took its votes to the APC. According to the court, a political party which sponsored a candidate who has allegedly defected is fully clothed with the requisite locus standi to bring a court action to compel the Speaker of the House of Representatives to declare the defecting member’s seat vacant. item.title: Policymakers must prioritise durable skills for future workplaces – HP Futures 2026 report
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande A new global report, HP Futures 2026, has urged policymakers in Nigeria and worldwide to prioritise durable skills such as creativity, critical thinking, communication and collaboration that will be essential in workplaces of the future. The report, led by HP, the Global Learning Council, and the Education Leaders Forum, convened 58 education, policymaking and future of work leaders globally to examine how education systems can equip young people for the future of work. The report called on policymakers to develop clear blueprints for helping students build durable skills and to ensure that these skills are not treated as secondary or extracurricular. According to the report, durable skills are becoming the core infrastructure of future readiness and must be resourced, timetabled and assessed accordingly. HP Futures 2026 recommends designing future skills-building programmes for public systems and low-resource contexts to ensure that durable skills do not become another source of inequality, through methods such as teacher-mediated AI, low-bandwidth delivery and predictable costs. It also called on policymakers to keep literacy, numeracy and identity-forming learning at the core of education, while using creative, hands-on approaches to deliver fundamentals and durable skills simultaneously. item.title: World Cup: FIFA suspends Egypt coach, forward for criticising referee after Argentina defeat
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has suspended Egypt coach Hossam Hassan for three matches and forward Mostafa Zico for five games following their criticism of the referee after the country’s 3-2 defeat by Argentina at the World Cup. According to Reuters, the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) announced the sanctions on Monday, adding that Egypt’s national team director, Ibrahim Hassan, the twin brother of Hossam, had also received a three-match suspension. Hossam was sanctioned for blaming refereeing errors for Egypt’s elimination from the tournament in the last 16, while Zico was punished for insulting the referee during a post-match interview. The EFA confirmed the disciplinary decisions in a statement, saying it had requested the detailed grounds for the sanctions from FIFA’s Disciplinary Committee to assess its legal options and determine whether to appeal. The controversy followed a disputed sequence of decisions during Egypt’s defeat to Argentina, with Zico having a goal disallowed for a foul in the build-up before Egypt’s players appealed for a penalty late in the match when the score was 2-2. However, FIFA refereeing chief Pierluigi Collina defended the officiating, warning that allegations against referees could expose them and their families to threats. The suspensions could affect Egypt’s preparations for their upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Malawi in November, with Hossam and Ibrahim Hassan potentially missing those fixtures and the opening match of the March international window. Zico’s five-match suspension could keep him out of action for Egypt until June. item.title: Imo Kidnap: Five Suspects Plead Not Guilty To Abducting Corps Members, Four Others
item.description: Five suspects accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and four other persons in Imo State have pleaded not guilty to the charges against them following their arraignment before the Justice Oputa State High Court in Owerri. The defendants face a three-count charge bordering on conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms. Three of the suspects — 25-year-old Usman Aliyu, also known as Chonge; 21-year-old Babangida Aliyu; and 23-year-old Mohammed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper — are accused of abducting the prospective corps members on October 1, 2026, Nigeria’s Independence Day. According to the charge sheet, the trio allegedly demanded and collected ₦48 million and an undisclosed amount in US dollars for the release of the victims. They were also accused of unlawfully possessing three AK-47 rifles, four magazines, a pistol and 81 rounds of live ammunition. The prosecuting counsel said the charge of conspiracy to commit hostage-taking is punishable under Section 6 of the Imo State Prohibition of Hostage Taking and Related Offences Law No. 4 of 2009. The other two defendants, 27-year-old Aminu Haliru and 20-year-old Tange Ibrahim, also known as Jijji, are accused of abducting four persons around Owerri and Mgbidi on October 4, four days after the first abduction. The prosecution alleged that Haliru, Ibrahim and other suspects still at large collected ₦8 million for the release of the four victims. They also face allegations of unlawfully possessing an AK-47 rifle and a pump-action gun. The presiding judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, adjourned the trial until Thursday, October 22, 2026. The victims were abducted by gunmen near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area on October 1, 2026, while travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The abduction sparked a security operation to locate the victims and apprehend those responsible. On October 7, the 20 prospective corps members and the civilian were rescued from the Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area. They subsequently received medical attention at the DSS hospital in Owerri. The DSS later arrested five suspects in intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Aba, Abia State. The operations involved a joint security team led by the DSS, working with the military, police and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for them and other fleeing members of the suspected kidnapping syndicate. The arraignment marks a further step in the investigation into the abduction, as the prosecution of the five arrested suspects gets underway. item.title: #EndSARS Anniversary: Police Fire Tear Gas To Disperse Gathering At Lekki Toll Gate
item.description: Tension flared at the Lekki Toll Gate as police fired tear gas to disperse activists and concerned Nigerians who gathered to commemorate the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests. The gathering was organised to honour those who lost their lives and remember the demonstrations against police brutality. The protesters were forced to flee as tear gas filled the area, disrupting the planned commemoration. Among those who gathered at the toll gate were the Lagos State governorship candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, and the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour. ﻿ Despite the disruption, the activists vowed to continue the struggle for justice and police reforms that inspired the #EndSARS protests, while keeping alive the memory of those who died. Tension has since subsided, and the area is now clear. Police operatives use teargas to disperse a gathering at the Lekki Toll Gate during the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests. Six years after the protests, the incident has renewed concerns about citizens’ right to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression. Tuesday’s incident comes six years after the protests that began in October 2020, as young Nigerians demanded an end to police brutality, particularly abuses associated with the now-disbanded Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS). Woman defies police teargas, honours #EndSARS victims on the sixth memorial at Lekki Tollgate The demonstrations spread across the country, with the Lekki Toll Gate becoming a focal point of the movement. On October 20, 2020, soldiers opened fire on protesters at the toll gate, an incident that remains a source of controversy over casualties and accountability. The Lagos State Judicial Panel of Inquiry, which investigated the incident, found that protesters were shot at, injured and killed. The state government later rejected key parts of the panel’s findings, including aspects of its conclusions on casualties. The anniversary has also been marked by clashes between security operatives and people who gathered at the toll gate in subsequent years. In October 2021, police fired tear gas during a memorial procession organised by youths and celebrities to honour victims of police brutality. The then Lagos Commissioner of Police, Hakeem Odumosu, said the officers were dispersing people he described as “miscreants”, rather than participants in the procession. In 2024, police again fired tear gas to disperse protesters marking the fourth anniversary. The protesters had called for the full implementation of recommendations made by judicial panels established after the 2020 demonstrations. The police said they acted after the protesters refused to disperse. The #EndSARS movement led to the disbandment of SARS in October 2020, but demands for accountability, compensation for victims and broader police reforms have continued.
